Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, has alleged that gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State repeatedly shouted his name and declared that they wanted to kill him. PUNCH Online reports that four members of Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation were reportedly killed. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general election on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, said he escaped because of the intervention of his Department of State Services escorts. He made the allegation on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, while recounting the attack on his campaign team in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The former lawmaker described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for attack when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. Omo-Agege said the gunmen opened fire less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the shooting started. Delta imposes 12-hour curfew in Ughelli north after rally violence ‘Rig and die’ rhetoric fuelling Delta tension – Keyamo Omo-Agege’s camp alleges four killed in Delta attack “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. He said four members of his campaign organisation were killed in the attack, while about 15 others sustained injuries, some of them critically. PUNCH Online had reported that Moses Anaughe, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly and a personal assistant to Omo-Agege, died at the Ughelli Central Hospital after he was reportedly shot during the attack. The campaign organisation had also said that four people were killed and four others injured in the incident. It identified another aide, Akima Efemena Umukoro, among the dead. In a statement issued on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, the campaign organisation described the incident as an assassination attempt on Omo-Agege during a campaign tour in Uduere. It alleged that armed men opened fire on the former deputy senate president and his entourage while he was addressing supporters. The organisation called on the Nigeria Police Force to conduct an independent and thorough investigation into the incident. It also appealed to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, the Independent National Electoral Commission, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters. The campaign organisation urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue.
